limitations: One account/region experiment; bounded absence is not permanent disappearance.

No conclusion about async deletion is made unless a positively observed blocker precedes admission, deletion completes before blocker runtime completion, and a retained-alias positive control executes.
Trail delivery is eventually consistent; missing records within polling bounds do not establish absence of AWS logging.
Request source identity and executed version are separately observed; no weighted routing or cross-account invocation exercised.

IAM-denied native API results are retained with real request IDs; any missing trail records are only absence under this owned-resource selector and delivery bound, not a conclusion that AWS never logs denials.
Asynchronous error destination may omit responsePayload and executedVersion; these native omissions were not filled with invented function errors.
Retry2 companion set retry/age/destination together and positively observed a Success destination before deletion, but did not establish an independent applied retry/age barrier.

findings: All twelve post-propagation successful API requests have actual delivered Invoke records correlated by SDK RequestId. Event requests additionally have correlated AWSService InvokeExecution records.

For unqualified requests functionName is the base ARN; explicit $LATEST, numeric and alias requests preserve qualification in functionName and include qualifier. InvokeExecution preserves the requested ARN in both functionName and sourceArn.

All retained Lambda data events use the base function ARN in resources. additionalEventData.functionVersion is an executed/resolved deployment ARN: $LATEST for latest requests and numeric1 for alias audit, independently from requested alias identity.

DryRun successful records also contain resolved functionVersion despite no runtime entry. Successful runtime-entry records contain customerEniId empty string; admission/DryRun and positively blocked dispatch examples omit it. Omission and null are preserved in raw records.

InvokeExecution also appears while a positive blocker prevents customer runtime entry. Deleted-alias failed dispatches instead produced AWSService Invoke with requestParameters null and no additionalEventData; they lack errorCode despite a correlated404 destination in the maxRetries0 case.

MaxRetries0 deleted-alias case positively delivered a404 RetriesExhausted destination preserving requested alias ARN. Retry2 companion establishes multiple native dispatch records, not a universal immediate-terminal rule.

Explicit $LATEST positively emits Resource=name:$LATEST and FunctionName+Resource=name:$LATEST+ExecutedVersion=$LATEST metric dimension sets. It does not fold entirely into the unqualified Resource=name identity.
